episodes.205340: An early September moisture surge resulted in the return of a more active weather pattern to Utah, including some isolated instances of flash flooding as well as a strong thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.205368: A surge in monsoon moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Lorena in the eastern Pacific combined with disturbances embedded in the northwest flow aloft resulting in a higher coverage of showers and thunderstorms across northern and central NM. Thunderstorms during the evening hours on September 5th resulted in flash flooding across the Pojoaque Pueblo between Santa Fe and Espanola.
episodes.205399: A potent cold front swept through Middle Tennessee during the evening of September 5, 2025. With an unstable and moist atmosphere ahead of this feature, the front provided additional lift to aid in the development of thunderstorms. These thunderstorms were able to become severe, producing large hail and damaging winds. The largest hail reported during this event was tennis ball size hail in Gainesboro with numerous reports of downed trees received throughout Middle Tennessee.
episodes.205614: Several widely scattered strong to severe thunderstorms produced gale- to storm-force winds over area waterways ahead of a cold front.
episodes.205615: A cold front spawned numerous showers and thunderstorms, a few of which became severe. A few instances of damaging wind gusts were noted over northern Virginia, near Washington, DC, and over northeastern Maryland.
episodes.205616: A cold front spawned numerous showers and thunderstorms, a few of which became severe. A few instances of damaging wind gusts were noted over northern Virginia, near Washington, DC, and over northeastern Maryland.
episodes.206058: A cold front moved through Southern New England in the afternoon bringing a round of severe storms which caused a wide swath of wind damage through MA with some in western CT. Some severe hail occurred in northern MA and a single storm dropped 5 tornadoes in central MA which led to widespread tree damage along but limited damage to structures.
episodes.206059: A cold front moved through Southern New England in the afternoon bringing a round of severe storms which caused a wide swath of wind damage through MA with some in western CT. Some severe hail occurred in northern MA and a single storm dropped 5 tornadoes in central MA which led to widespread tree damage along but limited damage to structures.
episodes.206491: A line of showers and storms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours over the Piedmont of North Carolina and Virginia. These storms tracked east into the mid to late evening hours, producing some isolated wind damage over Guilford and Forsyth Counties.
episodes.206510: Increasingly unstable atmospheric conditions on the afternoon of September 5th ahead of a cold front led to strong thunderstorms across portions of West Virginia. Storms initially developed west of the Ohio River and grew to strong to severe thresholds as they crossed into the state. As a result, damaging wind gusts that accompanied these storms caused a swath of downed trees across the Kanawha Valley and up into the central lowlands before weakening as they approached the Appalachian Mountains.
episodes.206516: Heavy monsoon rainfall caused some flooding in Yavapai County.
episodes.206629: A pseudo-warm front lifted up the Florida peninsula through the day. This lift combined with daytime heating and increased moisture produced isolated strong to pulse severe storms along the sea breezes and boundary mergers.
episodes.206725: Southwest flow aloft developed ahead of a longwave upper trough that entered portions of the Southern Plains and Ozarks region. This resulted in an increase in elevated moisture from the eastern Pacific, specifically from Hurricane Lorena, even as a weak cool front drifted southeast into portions of North Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, and Western Arkansas late in the day on September 5th. Ample Gulf moisture was present ahead of the front, with compressional warming contributing to strong instability as large scale forcing increased with the approaching front. As a result, scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed over portions of extreme Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, and Southwest Arkansas during the late evening into the early morning hours of the 5th-6th. One isolated severe thunderstorm producing damaging winds which downed a tree near Clarksville.
episodes.206726: Southwest flow aloft developed ahead of a longwave upper trough that entered portions of the Southern Plains and Ozarks region. This resulted in an increase in elevated moisture from the eastern Pacific, specifically from Hurricane Lorena, even as a weak cool front drifted southeast into portions of North Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, and Western Arkansas late in the day on September 5th. Ample Gulf moisture was present ahead of the front, with compressional warming contributing to strong instability as large scale forcing increased with the approaching front. As a result, scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed over portions of extreme Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, and Southwest Arkansas during the late evening into the early morning hours of the 5th-6th. These storms produced damaging winds which downed multiple trees across portions of Southwest Arkansas.
episodes.207273: As a cold front pushed east through central Kentucky, a line of scattered thunderstorms developed. One storm just north of the Tennessee border brought a few trees down as it moved east as another storm passing near Richmond blew trees down in an isolated area.
episodes.207374: Tropical Storm Lorena's remnants, a late-summer cold front, and an upper-level trough collectively contributed to significant thunderstorm activity across North Texas during the afternoon and evening of September 5th and into the morning of September 6th. Several of these storms generated damaging wind gusts and hail, while frequent cloud-to-ground lightning resulted in multiple residential fires.
episodes.207450: Thunderstorms, associated with a cold front, produced both damaging winds and flash flooding.
episodes.207572: Tropical moisture associated with a tropical wave and other trade wind perturbations, along with an upper-level trough resulted in the formation of strong showers and thunderstorms. These showers resulted in flooding, landslide and wind damage along portions of eastern, northern and western Puerto Rico.
episodes.207573: An isolated severe thunderstorm ahead of a cold front was able to become surface based and produce severe winds over a significant swath of Carter County, despite the early morning timeframe of the storm's passage.
episodes.207578: A cluster of very slow moving thunderstorms formed across eastern Lexington county, producing several areas of impactful flash flooding in West Columbia. With anomalously high precipitable water and weak shear, the cluster of storms moved very slowly over the course of several hours and dropped between 2-4 inches of rain in a highly urban area.
episodes.207630: An upper level trough approached from the west along with an associated surface cold front. The environment over the area ahead of the front was able to destabilize with MLCAPE values reaching about 2000 J/kg. This, combined with ample Effective Bulk Shear of about 45 kt, allowed severe thunderstorms to develop as the cold front moved through the area. These storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.207631: An upper level trough approached from the west along with an associated surface cold front. episodes.207632: An upper level trough approached from the west along with an associated surface cold front. episodes.207634: A brief waterspout was observed near Daytona Beach.
episodes.207661: A potent cold front quickly approached the Eastern Seaboard on September 6, pushing through central and eastern Virginia in the afternoon and evening hours. A line of showers and storms developed along and ahead of the front and produced gusty winds on the upper Chesapeake Bay as the line moved through.
episodes.207707: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front across eastern New York on September 6, 2025. One thunderstorm became severe downing trees and wires along its path across Columbia and northern portions of Dutchess counties.
episodes.207708: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front across northwestern Connecticut on September 6, 2025. One thunderstorm became severe downing trees and wires along its path. One tree fell onto a car injuring an occupant.
episodes.207709: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front across western Massachusetts on September 6, 2025. One thunderstorm became severe downing trees and wires along its path from Sheffield to Otis. A separate thunderstorm led to some downed trees south of Lenox.
episodes.207788: A boundary stretching from the southeastern Gulf across South Florida allowed for ample moisture to spread over the region which enabled the formation of showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.207790: A cold front slowly crossing the region resulted in a line of thunderstorms. A portion of this line in Central New Jersey produced severe winds.
episodes.207839: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed along a cold front across western North Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in the Mocksville area.
episodes.207840: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed along a cold front across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon and early evening. A few of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.207864: A late summer hot and unstable airmass was in place on the afternoon of September 6th across interior Maine.  A pre-frontal trough ahead of a surface cold front was approaching the state by the afternoon hours.  Discrete thunderstorms developed across Western Maine with most of them remaining below severe strength.  One stronger storm was able to produce damaging wind gusts in the Cumberland County Lakes Region.
episodes.207865: A late summer hot and unstable airmass was in place on the afternoon of September 6th across New Hampshire. A pre-frontal trough ahead of a surface cold front was approaching the state by the afternoon hours. Discrete thunderstorms developed across Central and Southern New Hampshire with most of them remaining below severe strength. A few storms became stronger and were able to produce damaging wind gusts and some large hail.
episodes.207866: A push of monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms, with the greatest activity on the 5th and 6th. Many storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.207868: A push of monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms, many of which produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.207877: A disorganized front brought thunderstorms across north and central Georgia through the afternoon hours of the 6th. A few storms became strong with one storm developing some 1 inch hail in the northwest Atlanta Metro.

An NWS survey team confirmed that a microburst produced a narrow swath of wind damage in the town of Gillham just south of the Kansas City Southern Railway to just east of Highway 71. The damage consisted almost entirely of uprooted hardwood and softwood trees, although a few softwood trees were also snapped. The damage was particularly concentrated just north of and down a hill from Gillham Baptist Church. The damage pattern was almost entirely unidirectional, pointing to the northeast, and even diverged slightly in a couple of places, which strongly indicated straight-line wind damage with estimated winds near 90 mph.

events.narrative: A thunderstorm produced an estimated wind gust to 34 knots (39 MPH) near the Herring Bay WeatherFlow sensor (XHEB).
In Sharon, a large tree was down across a driveway.
A Cocorahs observer measured 2.80 inches of rain at 4 NNW Paulden.  Minor flooding was reported over a private road near Feather Mountain Road.
A public weather station part of a mesonet network measured 3.69 inches in about 45  minutes. Rainfall started around 6:14 pm.
A public rain gage that is part of a mesonet network measured a daily storm total  rainfall of 4.32 inches along SE 108th Lane.  Rainfall started around 6:14 pm.
A public rain gage part of a mesonet network measured a daily storm total of 4.12 inches.  Rainfall started around 6:15 pm.

County comms reported multiple trees blown down, from southwest of Jonesville, ESE across mainly the north side of the city of Union, from Pineland Rd and Timberlake Rd southeast to Barnado Rd and Woodberry Dr.
County comms reported a tree blown down at Toney Rd & Meansville Rd and another tree down on Ingle Ave at Duncan Bypass.

Heavy rainfall resulted in the development of a flash flood and associated flood wave in Hurricane Wash. An emergency manager reported that a hiker within the wash was carried approximately 300 feet downstream before climbing a tree to escape the flood. Due to injuries, the hiker required helicopter evacuation for medical care. There were also washouts reported on Hole-in-the-Rock Road with seven vehicles reported stranded. Time of flood estimated based on radar.
Marion County Dispatch reported a tree was blown down into power lines in the Juniper  Court area.
Wires were blown down near the intersection of Highway 316 and NW 145th Avenue. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.
Vehicle reported to be submerged in flood waters at the intersection of Sunset Blvd and Raleigh St. Water was getting inside the vehicle.
Vehicle reported to be submerged in water at the corner of Sunset Blvd and 12th St.
Numerous roads were closed due to flash flooding.

Following heavy rains earlier in the afternoon, a landslide occurred along PR-4444 at km 1.0 in Barrio Cuchillas, Sector Loperena. Local authorities reported debris covering the roadway, prompting a temporary closure. Barricades and caution tape were placed to restrict traffic.

events.narrative: A trained spotter observed a waterspout that lasted less than sixty seconds within a shower northeast of Daytona Beach. Location estimated.
An NWS employee observed a SUV submerged in floodwaters on Chris Dr, near Augusta Rd. Police were on scene and had closed portions of Chris Dr.
Due to flash flooding, a vehicle was stranded in flood waters at Rt 35 and Clinton Ave.
